committedCopy: READ THE LABELS WITH CARE. This run was launched as a NOISE FLOOR -- main against itself at day and golden -- and both sides carry the label 'as shipped'. They are not the same build. The merge of origin/main into this branch landed in the served worktree while side A was shooting, so side A's page had already loaded c656249's js and side B loaded 13741fa's. The harness's own per-side build.sha1 is what caught it: A 4807b168 against B ae7b2be0, with identical GFX presets and identical authored triangles. So this is not a noise floor; it is an unplanned but valid c656249-vs-main A/B at day and golden, shot in one browser 25 minutes apart, and it is kept for that. The real noise floor is noise-floor-main-daygolden.report.json. AND THE TWO SIDES DID NOT LOAD THE SAME WAY. Side A took authoredReloads 2 and then the APARTMENTS.on poke -- the path night-compare.mjs's own comment calls unreliable -- and carries all four load warnings, ready in 379,315 ms. Side B took 0 reloads, no warnings, ready in 93,576 ms. A rebuild landing after the one-shot regime retint leaves new meshes day-coloured, so some unknown part of this A/B is a difference between the two SIDES rather than between the two builds. Everything the plan says about it is still true and still checked -- both frames fully settled, identical GFX presets, identical 2,600,942 authored triangles, 0 re-shoots -- but the recovery path is not identical, and the plan's own A9 box says a run like that 'is not this measurement'. Under the load-asymmetry rule added in the fifth pass this run is exit 2, and it is the only one of the ten kept here that the rule catches. Read the day/golden numbers as the shadow fix arriving WITH that confound attached, not as a clean two-build A/B. ||| SIXTH PASS, 2026-09-20 -- RE-MEASURED, NOT RE-SHOT. The two Capitol poses' `wall` and `dome` rectangles were on MapLibre's own fill-extrusions, not on anything we author: `--break slopes` deleted 3,560,273 triangles and every measured number at both poses came back bit-identical. wall and dome are now read off the A-vs-B mask of that run (92-96% of each rectangle is pixels the sabotage changed by more than 3 of 255 on any channel; 86-91% at a threshold of 6), the old rectangles are kept as `downtown`/`flanking` and declared `basemap`, and every kept report was re-measured from its OWN frames with --from against the corrected night-routes.json. No frame in this file was taken again; the frames are byte-for-byte the ones the shoot produced. Capitol numbers before and after are tabulated in docs/night-implementation-plan.md sec W0a. Every shot also gained `frame.bytes`/`frame.sha1`, and `report.exit` now exists in all ten files. It had never actually been re-measured under the loadAsymmetry rule the folder README says makes it exit 2, so the file said nothing of the kind. It has been now: `exit: 2` is in this file, with TWO asymmetry lines -- the reload path, and the new one, that both sides were shot against the same site and query and served DIFFERENT builds (A 4807b1680898, B ae7b2be0ceaf). That second line is the rebuild-landed-mid-run verdict, which until now was a thing a human had spotted off the overview sheet.
